blocks.text: The **genitive** does the work of English *of* and *'s*: **кни́га бра́т****а** — *(my) brother's book*, *the book of (my) brother*.
Masculine and neuter: **-а/-я**. Feminine: **-ы/-и** (the spelling rule makes **-и** after г, к, х, ж, ш, щ, ч).
Russian says *by me there is*: **У меня́ есть брат.** The owner goes in the genitive after **у**: у меня, у тебя, у него, у неё, у нас, у вас, у них — у Ива́н**а**, у ма́м**ы**.
To say something is *absent*, use **нет** and put the thing in the genitive: **У меня нет маши́ны.** *I have no car.* **Здесь нет метро́.** *There's no metro here.*
After **два, три, четы́ре** a noun is genitive singular (*два стол**а***); after **пять** and up, genitive plural (*пять стол**ов***).

exercises.q: У меня нет ___ . (время — time; it's neuter, genitive времени)

exercises.why: With **есть**, the thing you have stays in the **nominative**. Only the owner (у Анны) is genitive.
